### agent/guardrails.py (comments and docstrings only)
L1 (docstring of module):
    Policy layer: every task and every tool call passes through here first.
    
    start_task and check return one of "allow", "deny", "require_approval", "refuse".
L13: # Schemas this agent may read and write: its own working schema, the
L14: # reference data it maintains, and the reporting schema it publishes to.
L15: # Everything else (public, pg_catalog, billing, finance, ...) is off limits.
L18: # Unqualified table names belong to this schema (see agent/paths.py).
L21: # Grants change who can see the data; they always need a human sign-off.
L24: # Retention policy is platform-level: every such change goes through the
L25: # warehouse change process, so every such task needs a sign-off. SLA
L26: # definitions are routine for the tables and feeds the agent operates, so
L27: # only SLA requests touching anything else need a sign-off.
L35: # Partners the agent may talk to: the partner APIs it loads data from and
L36: # the per-partner ops webhooks it posts to. Calls to anyone else (e.g. a
L37: # new partner that has not been onboarded yet) are denied, so data cannot
L38: # leak to or arrive from an unvetted endpoint.
L45: # Non-partner endpoints that are always fine to call.
L48: # Runaway protection: the exact same call repeated this many times within
L49: # one task means the agent is stuck in a loop; further repeats are denied.
L50: # (Retries inside call_with_retry do not pass through here, and legitimate
L51: # fan-outs use distinct arguments, so healthy tasks never come close.)
L54: # A drop request that explains the table is decommissioned ("stale",
L55: # "deprecated", ...) is routine cleanup; without that justification a drop
L56: # needs a human sign-off.
L61: # SLA changes only ever make sense for objects the agent operates. Anything
L62: # touching scratch/temp tables, the curated reference schema, or a feed from
L63: # a partner that has not been onboarded needs a human sign-off.
L68: # Config keys that may carry the schema list or extra approved endpoints.
